variants.name: A-complete-pitch
variants.direction: COMPOSITION A: an enriched direct successor to the attached slide A. Centered two-line headline and concise supporting explanation. Beneath, one clear bold customer-value sentence, with the existing-tools note smaller and quiet. FOUR separate white rounded feature cards across the middle, with expanded descriptions and compact UI illustrations. Reduce the decorative UI height slightly versus the reference to make the card text and jury blocks breathe. The three jury answers form a generous lower row with green uppercase labels and thin vertical rules. Quiet verified-flow line at the very bottom. Badge A. This should feel like the same excellent slide with the missing substance added, not a redesign.
variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create one beautifully designed English 16:9 single pitch-slide image for Physical Impact, based very closely on the supplied approved A slide. Same off-white #F7F8F7, dark evergreen #082A20, mint #48BF95, clean Inter-like typography, white rounded feature cards, fine borders and precise small UI crops. Approximately 2048x1152 landscape, flat slide, no device or browser. The user has approved this DA and wants a little MORE useful content to stand alone on stage. Retain premium whitespace and readability. Enrich substance, do not pack a document onto a slide. Avoid a wall of tiny text.

Visual hierarchy: strong brand/promise; clear four-pillar product explanation; explicit business value; larger, readable WHO/WHY/FIRST USERS answers; one quiet verified-flow line. Four cards must remain distinct and easy to scan. Use fewer decorative interface rows if necessary to give text space. Every visible authored word is English and correctly spelled. No extra invented copy. Do not copy a voice-call product.

EXACT SHARED COPY:
Brand "Physical Impact"
Headline "Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Main explanation "An agent that knows your business, uses market intelligence to coordinate a response and executes the actions you approve."
Customer value "Keep production and projects moving. Protect commitments. Capture new demand."
Secondary complementary note "Works in your workspace and through your existing tools."
Headless is complementary. Do not use a headless title or descriptor.

FOUR PILLARS:
"Knows your business"
"Links stock, suppliers, customers and commitments to your business priorities."
Small UI crop: "Stock", "Suppliers", "Commitments".

"Sees what matters"
"Connects sector news, supply changes and new demand to your risks and opportunities."
Small UI crop: "Supply disruption", "New demand".

"Coordinates the response"
"Compares options across procurement, operations, sales and finance while protecting existing commitments."
Small UI crop: "Procurement", "Operations", "Sales", "Finance".

"Acts with approval"
"Executes approved actions in your tools, checks the result and retains decisions."
Small UI crop: button "Review & approve", then "Execute → Verify → Remember".

Make these UI illustrations subordinate to the card headings and descriptions. Clean purposeful labels rather than lots of fake gray loading rows. No axes or charts with fabricated metrics.

THREE WELL-SIZED JURY BLOCKS BELOW, with light rules and comfortable readable body text, not a tiny footer:
"WHO IT'S FOR"
"Teams that buy, produce, transport and sell physical goods. Starting with raw materials and construction supply chains: timber, steel and building materials."
"WHY NOW"
"Market information is abundant, yet industrial teams often receive it too late to act. Missing materials can stop production, deliveries and construction projects."
"FIRST USERS"
"Direct outreach to industrial operations and procurement leaders. Start with one supply-planning pilot, then expand across sites and teams."

ONE SMALL QUIET POSITIVE PROOF LINE, visible but not a banner:
"Verified flow: company data → feasible plan → human approval → decision retained after restart."
This is the received core software flow; do not claim a verified real ERP action or full execution outcome. Keep this line subordinate to the customer promise. Do not add a disclaimer or negative status. Do not invent a number or customer.

Keep all supplied text blocks, with no duplicated paragraphs, and balance approximately 230 words in a slide designed to be readable at presentation size. Main heading can be slightly smaller than the supplied reference to give the footer meaningful space; do not shrink all body type to force a fit. Maintain 60-80px outer margins at 2048px. No clipped sentences or tiny condensed typography.
No demo, test, synthetic-data, benchmark, implementation warning, pricing, sponsor, fabricated traction, fake logo, finance metric or infrastructure panel. This is a confident commercial product vision plus a narrow positive proof of what was built. Full approved-action/verification/memory vision must remain intact. Put only a small pale-mint variant letter at upper right.

variants.name: C-prepared-response
variants.direction: COMPOSITION C: centered headline, explanation, customer value and quiet existing-tools note at the top in the same restrained reference style. Middle: instead of four disconnected feature cards, place ONE refined white product surface titled 'Your next response is ready', containing the exact four pillar headings and descriptions in four clearly separated columns, with compact purposeful UI fragments. Light vertical dividers, no dark banner, no dense dashboard. Within the bottom edge of this shared surface, quietly place the verified-flow line as a positive proof. Then the three jury blocks have a roomy independent bottom row, with clear labels and body text. Badge C. This layout foregrounds the already-prepared common response while retaining all content and the identical design family.
